docs.title: Flask Campus
docs.text:
The Flask consumer layer for Campus apps: login/session context, request glue, the @journey decorator, and the audit middleware (request-span tracing + action journeys). Part of the Campus distribution split (campus#970) — apps install flask-campus and never a campus service or the storage/webauth core.

Current release: v0.2.1 · release notes in the changelog and on the releases page.

import flask
from campus.common import env
from campus.flask_campus import OAuthLoginManager, journey, audit

app = flask.Flask(__name__)
login_manager = OAuthLoginManager(default_endpoint="routes.landing")
login_manager.init_app(app)
audit.init_journeys(app)                     # episode plumbing: always on
if env.get_flag("AUDIT_TRACING_ENABLED", False):
    audit.init_tracing(app)                  # span capture: opt-in

@app.post("/assignments/<assignment_id>/send")
@login_manager.circle_member_required("timetable")
@journey("campus.submissions.submit")
def send_to_classroom(assignment_id: str): ...

docs.title: What's in the box
docs.text:
• Login manager & session context — OAuthLoginManager wires Google federated login into any Flask app and pushes the signed-in user onto flask.g per request; view decorators gate on sign-in and circle membership.
  • Audit middleware — audit.init_tracing captures request-response spans for the audit trail; audit.init_journeys groups related requests into user-action journeys; @journey labels them.
  • Views & request glue — typed view helpers (unpack_request, validate_json_response, ...), request/response types, and the OpenAPI generator core. See the reference.

Import paths are identical to the pre-split monorepo — the portions merge at import time. Span ingest, trace queries, and audit API-key management ship with the SDK as campus_python.audit; this dist ships no campus/audit portion.

docs.title: Boundary rules (enforced in this repo's tests)
docs.text:
• The consumer layer never imports campus services (campus.auth, campus.api, campus.audit, campus.yapper, campus.deploy, campus.config) — services import the consumer layer, never the reverse (#980).
  • It never imports the storage/webauth core (apps never touch them, #992).

docs.title: Audit middleware
docs.text:
campus.flask_campus.audit gives any Flask Campus app an audit trail: request-response spans for the audit service, and action journeys (#828) that group related requests — a page load, its XHRs and form posts, and the server-to-server calls they spawn — into one user-initiated episode.

The middleware moved here from campus.audit.middleware in flask-campus#31: it is request-scoped Flask glue, so it lives in the campus.flask_campus layer, while its HTTP client (span ingest, trace queries, API keys) ships with the SDK as campus_python.audit.

from campus.common import env
from campus.flask_campus import audit

audit.init_journeys(app)                     # always on — cheap plumbing
if env.get_flag("AUDIT_TRACING_ENABLED", False):
    audit.init_tracing(app)                  # opt-in per deployment

docs.title: Span capture: init_tracing
docs.text:
Registers before/after request hooks that open a span per request and ingest it asynchronously through campus_python.audit:

  • Trace identity: reuses X-Request-ID as trace id; the response echoes it back for correlation.
  • Rate gate: a fail-closed gate (opt-in with AUDIT_TRACING_FAIL_CLOSED=1) rejects requests rather than dropping spans when ingest is rate-limited (#831).
  • Warnings: WARNING+ records logged during a request ride on the span as redacted, capped tags.warnings, so incident triage doesn't need Railway stdout (#26). redact_sensitive is the shared producer-side scrub primitive — the same key list the audit service and retroactive scrub scripts use (#20).
  • Don't instrument the audit service itself — spans ingesting spans is infinite recursion.

Static files are skipped unless AUDIT_TRACING_INCLUDE_STATIC is set.

docs.title: Action journeys: init_journeys and @journey
docs.text:
init_journeys adopts or mints a journey id per request and keeps the campus_action_journey cookie alive, so a user episode stays one journey in the audit UI. Pass mint_on_navigation=False for services whose browser surface is the login flow itself (campus.auth) or that serve no browser pages (campus.api) — they adopt forwarded X-Journey-ID headers only.

The @journey decorator marks a view as a named action inside the journey:

@app.post("/assignments/<assignment_id>/send")
@journey("campus.submissions.submit")     # label convention: campus.<subject>.<action>
def send_to_classroom(assignment_id: str): ...

It works standalone too (without the journeys middleware): adopt the action cookie, else mint. fresh=True forces a new journey — a hard action boundary mid-episode.

docs.title: Propagation
docs.text: Either initializer installs the propagation seam: outbound SDK calls made while a request is being handled carry the span/journey/device headers this middleware stashed, keeping the audit waterfall intact across services. To instrument your own non-SDK requests.Session, use the SDK's instrument_requests_session.

docs.title: Minimal app
docs.text:
import flask
from campus.flask_campus import OAuthLoginManager

app = flask.Flask(__name__)
app.secret_key = "..."                 # sessions need a secret
login_manager = OAuthLoginManager(default_endpoint="routes.landing")
login_manager.init_app(app)

@app.route("/")
@login_manager.login_required
def index():
    return f"Hello, {flask.g.user.email}"

init_app registers an auth blueprint (/auth/login, /auth/finalize, /auth/logout) and a before-request hook that resolves the session cookie to flask.g.user. The default endpoint is addressed as blueprint.endpoint (routes.landing = the landing view in the routes blueprint).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The default Campus client resolves from the environment (see the SDK's configuration guide):

Variable Used for CLIENT_ID / CLIENT_SECRET server-mode Campus client (login flows, API calls as the client) ACCESS_TOKEN bearer alternative for the audit client AUDIT_API_KEY audit span ingest (with tracing enabled) AUDIT_TRACING_ENABLED gate: call audit.init_tracing only when set AUDIT_TRACING_FAIL_CLOSED fail-closed audit rate gate (opt-in) AUDIT_TRACING_INCLUDE_STATIC capture spans for static-file requests (default off)

Pass campus_client= to OAuthLoginManager to share an existing campus_python.Campus instance instead.

docs.title: Adding gated views
docs.text:
@app.route("/admin")
@login_manager.circle_member_required("campus-admin")
def admin_panel(): ...

@app.route("/timetable/edit")
@login_manager.circle_admin_required("timetable")   # gates on timetable.admin
def edit_timetable(): ...

Circle gates check membership through campus.api circles (cached 60s), redirect signed-out users to sign-in, 403 non-members, and fail closed with 503 if the circles backend cannot answer. Enforcement lives in campus.api — these gates render the right UI, they are never the only protection for data.

docs.title: Login & sessions
docs.text:
OAuthLoginManager is the one object that wires Campus identity into a Flask app. It bundles three things:

  1. an auth blueprint with /auth/login, /auth/finalize, and /auth/logout views (Google federated login against Campus Auth);
  2. a before-request context hook that resolves the session cookie to a user object and pushes it onto flask.g.user (via campus.flask_campus.context.push_context, with a process-local UserCache so warm requests skip upstream calls);
  3. view decorators for gating: login_required, circle_member_required, and circle_admin_required.
login_manager = OAuthLoginManager(
    default_endpoint="routes.landing",   # redirect target after login/logout
    login_scopes=None,                   # default ["campus.profile"]
)
login_manager.init_app(app)              # Flask app or blueprint

login_scopes requests management scopes for the minted user token (#865/#883 two-leg model). Apps that pass anything beyond the default must extend their OAuth client's allowed_scopes allowlist before deploying — campus.auth validates against that cap fail-closed.

docs.title: How a request gets its user
docs.text:
• Signed-in: flask.g.user is a Campus user object; g.user.email is also the name of the user's own circle (their identity in the access model). Snapshots in UserCache are rehydrated per hit, so callers cannot poison the cache by mutating g.user.
  • Signed-out: flask.g.user is absent (getattr(flask.g, "user", None) is the idiom). Gated views redirect to sign-in with ?next= the original path; ungated views run anonymously.
  • The SDK's legacy flask.session reads stay compatible: install_session_provider() points the SDK's sessionstore at the same session keys (the login manager installs this for you).

docs.title: Gating reference
docs.text:
Decorator Effect login_required redirect signed-out users to sign-in circle_member_required(circle) + 403 for signed-in non-members, 503 if the circles backend is unreachable (fail closed) circle_admin_required(resource) sugar for circle_member_required(f"{resource}.admin")

All three fold the sign-in redirect in, so decorator stacking order never matters. Enforcement stays in campus.api: a circle gate renders the right UI before the API's 403 wall — it must never be the only protection for data.

docs.title: Journeys on login flows
docs.text: Services whose browser surface is the login flow (campus.auth) or that serve no browser pages (campus.api) initialize journeys with mint_on_navigation=False so navigation events don't mint journeys; they adopt forwarded X-Journey-ID headers only. See Audit middleware.

docs.title: campus.flask_campus.audit
docs.text:
campus.flask_campus.audit

Audit middleware for Flask-based Campus apps: automatic span capture for HTTP requests and the action-journey lifecycle (#828) that groups related requests into user-initiated episodes.

Moved from campus.audit.middleware (flask-campus#31): the middleware is request-scoped Flask glue, so it lives in the flask_campus layer, while its HTTP client (span ingest, trace queries, API keys) ships with the SDK as campus_python.audit.

Span capture is opt-in per deployment: call init_tracing only when AUDIT_TRACING_ENABLED and AUDIT_API_KEY are configured. Journey adoption/minting is cheap request-scoped plumbing and stays always-on (recording is a no-op when tracing is off).

Note: init_tracing should only be called for Flask deployments that are not the audit service itself (to avoid infinite recursion).

The producer-side scrub primitive is public interface — the audit service and the retroactive scrub script on campus reuse the same key list, so keyed redaction cannot drift between writer and scrubber. The lazy import mirrors init_tracing: tracing loads at middleware-setup time, not package-import time.

def __getattr__(name: str):
    """Lazily expose ``redact_sensitive`` (flask-campus#20).

    The producer-side scrub primitive is public interface — the audit
    service and the retroactive scrub script on campus reuse the same
    key list, so keyed redaction cannot drift between writer and
    scrubber. The lazy import mirrors init_tracing: tracing loads at
    middleware-setup time, not package-import time.
    """
    if name == "redact_sensitive":
        from .tracing import redact_sensitive
        return redact_sensitive
    raise AttributeError(f"module {__name__!r} has no attribute {name!r}")

def init_tracing(app: flask.Flask) -> None:
    """Initialize tracing middleware for the Flask app.

    Registers before_request and after_request hooks to capture
    request-response data as spans.

    Note: Should only be called for campus.auth and campus.api deployments,
    not for campus.audit (to avoid infinite recursion).

    Args:
        app: The Flask application to instrument.
    """
    from . import tracing

    _install_propagation()
    tracing.install_warning_collector()

    @app.before_request
    def audit_rate_gate():
        """Fail-closed gate for audit ingest rate limiting (#831).

        Registered before start_span so a gated (503) request never
        opens a span. No-op unless AUDIT_TRACING_FAIL_CLOSED=1.
        """
        return tracing.check_rate_gate()

    @app.before_request
    def start_span():
        """Start a root span for each incoming request.

        Generates or reuses trace_id from X-Request-ID header.
        Stores timing and identifier data in flask.g for use in after_request.
        """
        tracing.start_span()

    @app.after_request
    def end_span(response):
        """Complete the span and send to audit service.

        Builds TraceSpan from request-response data and ingests asynchronously.
        Echoes trace_id in response headers for correlation.

        Args:
            response: The Flask response object.

        Returns:
            The response with X-Request-ID header added.
        """
        return tracing.end_span(response)

docs.title: redact_sensitive(value: typing.Any) -> typing.Any
docs.text:
Mask values stored under sensitive keys, recursively (#805).

Keyed redaction only: scalars and free-text bodies pass through unchanged — text scrubbing needs sensitive-data marking (#806). Email keys are value-aware: workspace-domain addresses pass through (campus#1125 ruling), everything else under them is masked. Returns a new structure; the input is not mutated.

Source code in src/campus/flask_campus/audit/tracing.py 
def redact_sensitive(value: typing.Any) -> typing.Any:
    """Mask values stored under sensitive keys, recursively (#805).

    Keyed redaction only: scalars and free-text bodies pass through
    unchanged — text scrubbing needs sensitive-data marking (#806).
    Email keys are value-aware: workspace-domain addresses pass through
    (campus#1125 ruling), everything else under them is masked.
    Returns a new structure; the input is not mutated.
    """
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {
            key: (
                _REDACTED
                if _is_sensitive_key(key)
                else (
                    _REDACTED
                    if _is_pii_email_key(key)
                    and not _is_workspace_email(item)
                    else redact_sensitive(item)
                )
            )
            for key, item in value.items()
        }
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [redact_sensitive(item) for item in value]
    return value

def get_request_payload() -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Get the JSON payload from the Flask request."""
    if not flask.has_request_context():
        raise (
            RuntimeError("No Flask request context available")
        ) from None
    if flask.request.method == "GET":
        return dict(flask.request.args)

    # Bodyless requests (no Content-Type, empty body) are common for
    # DELETE calls from API clients (campus_python/campus-cli send
    # DELETE without a body), so treat them as an empty payload.
    if not flask.request.get_data(cache=True):
        return {}

    json_payload = flask.request.get_json(silent=True)
    if json_payload is None:
        raise api_errors.InvalidRequestError(
            message="Malformed JSON payload",
            error_code="MALFORMED_REQUEST",
            # Error details must stay JSON-serializable; the raw body is bytes
            body=flask.request.data.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"),
        ) from None
    if not isinstance(json_payload, dict):
        raise api_errors.InvalidRequestError(
            message="Expected object in JSON payload",
            body=json_payload,
        ) from None
    return json_payload

docs.text:
Unpack request arguments into the given function's arguments, based on its signature.

String values (query/path parameters) are coerced to the annotated int/float/bool type; a failed coercion is reported as a field error.

Raises ValidationError with structured field errors for any issues.

Source code in src/campus/flask_campus/utils.py 
def unpack_into(
        func: Callable[..., Any],
        **request_args: Any,
) -> Any:
    """Unpack request arguments into the given function's arguments,
    based on its signature.

    String values (query/path parameters) are coerced to the annotated
    int/float/bool type; a failed coercion is reported as a field error.

    Raises ValidationError with structured field errors for any issues.
    """
    reconciled, extra_args, missing_params = parameter.reconcile(
        request_args,
        func
    )

    field_errors: list[FieldError] = []

    # Check if function accepts **kwargs
    func_params = inspect.signature(func).parameters
    has_var_keyword = any(
        p.kind == inspect.Parameter.VAR_KEYWORD
        for p in func_params.values()
    )

    # Only raise error for extra arguments if function doesn't have **kwargs
    if extra_args and not has_var_keyword:
        field_errors.extend([
            FieldError(
                field=param,
                code="UNRECOGNIZED_FIELD",
                message=f"Unexpected field: {param}"
            )
            for param in extra_args
        ])

    if missing_params:
        field_errors.extend([
            FieldError(
                field=param,
                code="MISSING",
                message=f"Missing required field: {param}"
            )
            for param in missing_params
        ])

    for name, value in reconciled.items():
        param = func_params.get(name)
        if param is None or parameter.is_variadic(param):
            continue
        try:
            reconciled[name] = _coerce_str_value(value, param.annotation)
        except ValueError:
            field_errors.append(FieldError(
                field=name,
                code="INVALID_TYPE",
                message=f"Expected {param.annotation} for field: {name}"
            ))

    # Reject values whose type does not match the annotation, so that
    # e.g. a string scopes field is not silently iterated char-by-char
    for name, value in reconciled.items():
        param = func_params.get(name)
        if param is None or parameter.is_variadic(param):
            continue
        compatible = _is_type_compatible(value, param.annotation)
        if compatible is None:
            continue
        if compatible:
            reconciled[name] = _coerce_to_annotation(value, param.annotation)
        else:
            field_errors.append(FieldError(
                field=name,
                code="INVALID_TYPE",
                message=f"Invalid type for field: {name}"
            ))

    if field_errors:
        raise ValidationError(
            message="One or more fields are invalid",
            errors=field_errors
        )

    # Call the original function with unpacked arguments
    # Include extra_args only if function has **kwargs
    return func(**reconciled, **extra_args)

def unpack_request(
        func: Callable[..., Any]
) -> Callable[[], Any]:
    """Decorator that unpacks Flask request into the decorated function's
    arguments, based on its signature.

    GET requests will use URL parameters, POST/PUT requests will use JSON body.
    """
    # Validate func annotations
    if not func.__annotations__:
        raise (
            ValueError(f"Function {func.__name__} missing type annotations")
        ) from None
    incompatible_params = [
        param for param in inspect.signature(func).parameters.values()
        if not parameter.is_keyword_supported(param)
    ]
    if incompatible_params:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Parameters {incompatible_params} must be "
            "keyword-argument-compatible"
        ) from None

    @wraps(func)
    def wrappervf(*args, **kwargs) -> Any:
        """The view function presented to Flask"""
        assert not args, f"Positional arguments not supported: {args}"
        request_args = get_request_payload()
        return unpack_into(func, **kwargs, **request_args)

    return wrappervf

def validate_request_and_extract_json(
        schema: Mapping[str, Type], *,
        on_error: types.ErrorHandler,
) -> types.JsonObject:
    """Validate the request JSON body against the provided schema before
    returning the payload.
    """
    try:
        payload = get_request_payload()
        record.validate_keys(
            payload,
            schema,
        )
    except (KeyError, TypeError, JSONDecodeError) as err:
        on_error(400, message=err.args[0])
    else:
        return payload

def validate_json_response(
        schema: Mapping[str, Type],
        resp_json: Mapping[str, Any], *,
        on_error: types.ErrorHandler,
        ignore_extra: bool = True,
        error_status_code: types.StatusCode = 500,
        error_message: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Validate the response JSON body against the provided schema."""
    if resp_json is None:
        on_error(500, message="Response body must be a JSON object")

Action-journey decorator for client apps (#828).

One decorator is the entire API surface app authors touch:

from campus import flask_campus

@app.post("/assignments/submit")
@flask_campus.journey("campus.submissions.submit")
def submit_assignment(): ...

@journey names the user action the view serves. Names follow the yapper emission convention (campus.<subject>[.<sub>].<action>) and reuse the same labels (#840): an emission is the event an episode culminates in, so a journey named campus.submissions.submit reads as "the episode that ended in that emission". Mint a new label (same format) only when no emission exists for the action. The journey id itself is adopted from the active request when one exists (the journeys middleware's cookie/header adoption, or a previous hop of the same episode) and minted fresh only when there is none — so decorating a view is always safe, never fragments an ongoing episode, and requires no knowledge of ids, cookies, or headers. fresh=True opts out of adoption for a hard action boundary mid-episode.

Journeys are observability correlation, not application state: if audit tracing is disabled the decorator still runs but nothing is recorded.

def journey(
        name: str | None = None,
        *,
        fresh: bool = False,
) -> typing.Callable:
    """Mark a view as part of a (named) user-action journey.

    Args:
        name: Label for the journey, following the yapper emission
            convention (``campus.<subject>[.<sub>].<action>``) and
            reusing the emission label where one exists (#840); lands
            in the span's tags.journey_name for the journey view cards.
        fresh: Start a NEW journey for this request even if one is
            active — a hard action boundary mid-episode. Default False:
            adopt the active journey, minting only when there is none.

    Returns:
        The decorated view.
    """
    def decorator(view):
        @wraps(view)
        def wrapped(*args, **kwargs):
            """Resolve the journey id, stamp g, then run the view."""
            journey_id = getattr(flask.g, "journey_id", None)
            if not journey_id:
                # Standalone use (no journeys middleware): adopt the
                # action cookie, else mint.
                journey_id = (
                    flask.request.cookies.get(
                        ACTION_JOURNEY_COOKIE
                    )
                    or uid.generate_category_uid("journey")
                )
            elif fresh:
                journey_id = uid.generate_category_uid("journey")
            flask.g.journey_id = journey_id
            if name:
                flask.g.journey_name = name
            # Continue the episode after this response (redirects,
            # same-page XHRs) even without the journeys middleware.
            flask.after_this_request(_set_journey_cookie)
            return view(*args, **kwargs)
        return wrapped
    return decorator

campus.flask_campus.circles

Circles-backed membership checks for Flask views.

This module answers "is the signed-in user in this circle" for view gates (OAuthLoginManager.circle_member_required), resolving membership the same way campus.api's own enforcement does: the caller's user ID (their email, which is also their user circle's name) against the target circle's members. It is view-level gating only — campus.api remains the enforcement point for the resources themselves; this gate exists so apps can render the right UI before the API's 403 wall.

Checks run as the signed-in user (campus.with_user_session), not with the app's client credentials: client principals hold no domain authority, and circle reads are only open "for now".

Membership answers are cached process-local per (circle, user) for a short TTL — warm admin views make zero upstream calls. Definitive non-membership (absent member, missing circle) fails closed with False; infrastructure failures raise CirclesUnavailableError so the caller can distinguish a 403 from a degraded backend.

class MembersCache:
    """Process-local cache of membership answers.

    Keys are (circle_name, user_id) pairs; values are
    (expires_at, is_member). Expired entries are dropped lazily on
    read. Answers only — never the members dict itself: transitive
    resolution (a stated campus.api refinement) changes which users
    count as members, so caching raw membership data would drift.
    """

    def __init__(self, ttl_seconds: float = CIRCLE_MEMBERS_TTL_SECONDS):
        self.ttl_seconds = ttl_seconds
        self._entries: dict[
            tuple[str, str],
            tuple[float, bool],
        ] = {}

    def get(self, circle: str, user_id: str) -> bool | None:
        """The cached answer for (circle, user), or None on miss/expiry."""
        entry = self._entries.get((circle, user_id))
        if entry is None:
            return None
        expires_at, is_member = entry
        if time.monotonic() >= expires_at:
            self._entries.pop((circle, user_id), None)
            return None
        return is_member

    def put(self, circle: str, user_id: str, is_member: bool) -> None:
        """Cache the membership answer for ttl_seconds."""
        self._entries[(circle, user_id)] = (
            time.monotonic() + self.ttl_seconds,
            is_member,
        )

def is_member(
        campus: _WithUserSession,
        cache: MembersCache,
        circle: str,
        user_id: str,
) -> bool:
    """True if `user_id` is a member of the named circle.

    The circle is resolved by name (names are unique best-effort and
    stable — role circles use dotted names like "timetable.admin";
    user circles are named after the email account, and user IDs are
    emails, so the lookup key is the caller's ID verbatim). A missing
    circle denies fail-closed with a warning — that is a bootstrap
    problem, not a per-user denial.

    Raises:
        CirclesUnavailableError: If the circles backend (or the user
            token flow backing the check) fails to answer.
    """
    cached = cache.get(circle, user_id)
    if cached is not None:
        return cached
    try:
        with campus.with_user_session() as client:
            matches = [
                c for c in client.api.circles.list()
                if c.name == circle
            ]
            if not matches:
                logger.warning(
                    "No circle named '%s' is configured: denying "
                    "membership fail-closed — run the circles "
                    "bootstrap (docs/circles-access-control.md)",
                    circle,
                )
                answer = False
            else:
                # The single-membership probe (campus#1098): the
                # server's answer to "is this principal in this
                # circle" — client checks keep resolving membership in
                # exactly one place when campus.api adds access tiers
                # or transitive resolution. 404 (absent member) is the
                # expected negative answer; other errors surface.
                answer = (
                    client.api.circles[matches[0].id].members.get(user_id)
                    is not None
                )
    except CirclesUnavailableError:
        raise
    except Exception as err:
        logger.error("Circle membership check failed: %s", err)
        raise CirclesUnavailableError(
            f"Could not answer membership in '{circle}': {err}"
        ) from err
    cache.put(circle, user_id, answer)
    return answer

def reconcile(
        request_args: dict[str, typing.Any],
        func: typing.Callable[..., typing.Any],
        allow_extra: bool = False,
) -> tuple[dict[str, typing.Any], dict[str, typing.Any], list[str]]:
    """Reconcile request arguments with function parameters. Returns a
    tuple of:
    - reconciled arguments (with defaults applied)
    - extra arguments (not in function parameters)
    - missing required parameters

    Args:
        request_args: The arguments from the request (e.g., URL params)
        func: The function whose parameters to reconcile against
        allow_extra: Whether to allow extra arguments not in params
                     if True, they are included in reconciled args
                     if False, they are returned in extra_args
    """
    func_params = dict(inspect.signature(func).parameters)
    MISSING: object = object()
    reconciled: dict[str, typing.Any] = {}
    extra_args: dict[str, typing.Any] = {}
    missing_params: list[str] = []
    for name, param in func_params.items():
        arg = request_args.get(name, MISSING)
        if is_variadic(param):
            # Variadic parameter (*args, **kwargs): only include if
            # present and non-empty
            if arg is not MISSING and arg != {} and arg != ():
                reconciled[name] = arg
        elif is_optional(param):
            # Optional parameter: use default if missing, otherwise use
            # provided value
            reconciled[name] = param.default if arg is MISSING else arg
        else:
            # Required parameter: must be present in request_args
            if arg is MISSING:
                missing_params.append(name)
            else:
                reconciled[name] = arg
    extra_args = {k: v for k, v in request_args.items()
                  if k not in func_params}
    if allow_extra:
        reconciled.update(extra_args)
        extra_args = {}
    return reconciled, extra_args, missing_params

campus.flask_campus.openapi

OpenAPI 3 generator for Campus Flask services (campus#1029).

Each service serves a public, unauthenticated OpenAPI 3 JSON at /{service-prefix}/openapi.json behind campus-gateway. The spec is generated from the Flask app object and committed as a campus/{service}/docs/openapi.json artifact (regenerate with the CLI below; drift and version-pinning unit tests enforce the regenerate-and-bump discipline).

Two halves, deliberately separable:

  • Schema emitter: functools.singledispatch over campus.common.schema types (Email, DateTime, CampusID, String, Integer, Boolean, Array, Object, ...) and builtin fallbacks, producing plain JSON-Schema dicts. Dispatch lives entirely in the generator — campus.common.schema stays spec-agnostic.
  • App introspector: walks app.url_map (Flask converter → OpenAPI parameter), introspects view signatures (annotations → parameters, defaults → optional), and uses docstrings as the operation documentation: the first line becomes summary and the remainder becomes description. There are no overlay files; the error-envelope components are generated once from the campus.common.errors.api_errors taxonomy (#714).

Parameter extraction follows the flask_campus.unpack_request signature conventions: GET handlers receive query parameters, all other methods receive a JSON body; path parameters come from the URL rule; a parameter without a default is required. Parameters read from flask.request directly (outside unpack_request) are invisible to the generator.

This module is the pure generator core: it imports nothing from the services repo, so it moves with the flask-campus carve (#993) untouched. The AppModule-to-app convenience (build_spec_from_module) lives in campus.deploy beside create_app — the legal import direction is service-repo glue importing the consumer layer, never the reverse. The regen entrypoint is scripts/generate_openapi.py in the services repo (generation builds the service app, so it needs that repo's environment).

Usage::

from campus.flask_campus import openapi
spec = openapi.generate_spec(
    app, title="Campus Auth API", version="0.2.0",
)
openapi.write_spec(spec, "campus/auth/docs/openapi.json")

Version pinning: version is explicit and required — the generator never guesses whose release it is pinning. The services repo pins the campus-suite version from its pyproject.toml; a PR that changes the spec must regenerate the artifact and bump that version (minor for spec changes, patch for API-preserving changes).

Security schemes (bearer/apikey gates) are a phase-2 item and are not emitted yet; response bodies are documented generically (200 + default error envelope).

def annotation_to_schema(annotation: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Emit an OpenAPI schema dict for a type annotation.

    Handles the typing constructs that appear in view signatures
    (``X | None`` unions, ``Literal[...]``, ``list[T]``, ``dict[K, V]``)
    and delegates concrete classes to the emitter.
    """
    if annotation is inspect.Parameter.empty or annotation is Any:
        return {}
    if annotation is None or annotation is type(None):
        return {"nullable": True}
    origin = typing.get_origin(annotation)
    if origin is Union or origin is UnionType:
        members = list(typing.get_args(annotation))
        non_none = [m for m in members if m is not type(None)]
        if len(non_none) == 1:
            merged = annotation_to_schema(non_none[0])
            if len(non_none) != len(members):
                merged = dict(merged)
                merged["nullable"] = True
            return merged
        return {"anyOf": [annotation_to_schema(m) for m in members]}
    if origin is Literal:
        literal: dict[str, Any] = {"enum": list(typing.get_args(annotation))}
        value_types = {type(v) for v in typing.get_args(annotation)}
        if value_types and value_types <= {str}:
            literal["type"] = "string"
        elif value_types and all(isinstance(v, bool) for v in typing.get_args(annotation)):
            literal["type"] = "boolean"
        elif value_types and value_types <= {int}:
            literal["type"] = "integer"
        elif value_types and value_types <= {float}:
            literal["type"] = "number"
        return literal
    if origin is list:
        args = typing.get_args(annotation)
        items = annotation_to_schema(args[0]) if args else {}
        return {"type": "array", "items": items}
    if origin is dict:
        args = typing.get_args(annotation)
        obj: dict[str, Any] = {"type": "object"}
        if len(args) == 2 and args[1] is not Any:
            obj["additionalProperties"] = annotation_to_schema(args[1])
        return obj
    if isinstance(annotation, type):
        return _emit_for_class(annotation)
    return {}

def generate_spec(
        app: flask.Flask,
        *,
        title: str,
        description: str = "",
        version: str,
        exclude_endpoints: Iterable[str] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Generate an OpenAPI 3 spec dict from a Flask app object.

    Walks ``app.url_map``; every non-excluded rule becomes a path item,
    every method an operation. ``version`` is required and lands in
    ``info.version`` verbatim — callers pass the release they are
    pinning. The 308 trailing-slash convention is appended to the
    description unless the description already mentions it.
    """
    excluded = (
        DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_ENDPOINTS if exclude_endpoints is None
        else frozenset(exclude_endpoints)
    )
    selected: list[tuple[routing.Rule, str]] = []
    for rule in app.url_map.iter_rules():
        leaf = rule.endpoint.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
        if leaf in excluded:
            continue
        for method in sorted((rule.methods or set()) - {"HEAD", "OPTIONS"}):
            selected.append((rule, method))

    operation_ids = _operation_ids(selected)

    paths: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    tags: set[str] = set()
    for rule, method in selected:
        view = app.view_functions[rule.endpoint]
        operation = _build_operation(rule, method, view)
        operation["operationId"] = operation_ids[(rule.endpoint, method, rule.rule)]
        tag = _endpoint_tag(rule.endpoint)
        if tag:
            operation["tags"] = [tag]
            tags.add(tag)
        path_item = paths.setdefault(_to_openapi_path(rule.rule), {})
        path_item[method.lower()] = operation

    if description and "308" not in description:
        description = f"{description}\n\n{_TRAILING_SLASH_NOTE}"
    elif not description:
        description = _TRAILING_SLASH_NOTE

    error_schemas, error_responses = _error_components()
    return {
        "openapi": "3.0.3",
        "info": {
            "title": title,
            "description": description,
            "version": version,
        },
        "tags": [{"name": tag} for tag in sorted(tags)],
        "paths": paths,
        "components": {
            "schemas": error_schemas,
            "responses": error_responses,
        },
    }

            default_endpoint: Default endpoint to redirect to after login/logout

                minted user credential (rides start_login's scopes
                parameter). None keeps ["campus.profile"]. Apps whose
                features need management scopes on the user's token
                (#865/#883 two-leg model) pass the full list — and
                must extend their client's allowed_scopes cap BEFORE
                deploying, since campus.auth validates the request
                against that cap fail-closed.

    def _push_context_hook(self) -> None:
        """App-wide before_request hook that pushes the auth context.

        Static asset requests never read g.user, so they skip the
        upstream auth lookup (#689): a session-carrying browser
        otherwise pays push_context's auth API calls on every stylesheet
        and script, which can wedge a sync worker under load.
        """
        endpoint = flask.request.endpoint or ""
        if endpoint == "static" or endpoint.endswith(".static"):
            return
        context.push_context(self.campus, self._cache)

        # Span identity (#820): the audit tracing middleware reads
        # g.user_id / g.client_id when building this request's span.
        # Page loads are the waterfall roots, so stamping them here is
        # what lets the audit UI attribute a page load to the app's
        # client and the signed-in user.
        user = getattr(flask.g, "user", None)
        if user is not None and getattr(user, "id", None):
            flask.g.user_id = user.id
        client_id = env.get("CLIENT_ID")
        if client_id:
            flask.g.client_id = client_id

            self._push_context_hook, self.campus, self._cache,
            self.default_endpoint, login_scopes=self.login_scopes,
        )
        app.register_blueprint(bp)
        if isinstance(app, flask.Flask):
            app.before_request(self._push_context_hook)
        elif isinstance(app, flask.Blueprint):
            app.before_app_request(self._push_context_hook)

        @wraps(view)

            if not hasattr(flask.g, "user") or flask.g.user is None:
                return flask.redirect(
                    flask.url_for('auth.login', next=flask.request.path)
                )
            return view(*args, **kwargs)
        return wrapped_view

        """Decorator: the view requires membership in a named circle.

        View-level gating over campus.api circles (the domain access
        control): the signed-in user's ID — their email, which is also
        their user circle's name — must be a member of `circle`
        (e.g. "campus-admin" or a role circle "timetable.admin"). Use
        circle_admin_required for the per-resource admin roles.

        UI before the API's 403 wall and must never be the only
        protection for data.

        behaviour, folded in so decorator stacking order never
        matters). Signed-in non-members get 403 — they are
        authenticated, not unknown. If the circles backend cannot
        answer (network, API error), the view fails closed with 503
        rather than a misleading 403; answers are cached briefly
        (circles.MembersCache) so warm views make no upstream calls.
        """
        def decorator(view: Callable) -> Callable:
            @wraps(view)
            def wrapped_view(*args, **kwargs):
                """Gate the view on sign-in + circle membership."""
                user = getattr(flask.g, "user", None)
                if user is None:
                    return flask.redirect(
                        flask.url_for('auth.login', next=flask.request.path)
                    )
                user_id = getattr(user, "id", None)
                if not user_id:
                    flask.abort(403, description=(
                        "Signed-in identity has no user ID; membership "
                        f"in '{circle}' cannot be verified."
                    ))
                try:
                    member = circles.is_member(
                        self.campus, self._circle_cache, circle, user_id
                    )
                except circles.CirclesUnavailableError as err:
                    flask.current_app.logger.error(
                        "Circle membership unavailable: %s", err
                    )
                    flask.abort(503, description=(
                        "Authorization backend unavailable; "
                        "try again shortly."
                    ))
                if not member:
                    flask.abort(403, description=(
                        f"Membership in the '{circle}' circle is required."
                    ))
                return view(*args, **kwargs)
            return wrapped_view
        return decorator

    def circle_admin_required(self, resource: str) -> Callable:
        """Decorator: the view requires the <resource>.admin role.

        Convenience over circle_member_required for the circles
        bootstrap's per-resource role circles: circle_admin_required(
        "timetable") gates on membership in the "timetable.admin"
        circle — the same role campus.api's mutation routes enforce
        server-side (campus/api/authz.py require_resource_admin).
        """
        return self.circle_member_required(f"{resource}.admin")

campus.flask_campus.context

Auth session-context mechanics for Flask hosts.

This module owns the client-side half of the campus login flow: the storage of the auth-session and login-session ids (flask.session, via the SDK's SESSION_STORAGE_KEY / LOGIN_STORAGE_KEY), the request-entry context push (g.user / g.device with a per-manager user cache), and the login-flow steps (start / finalize / logout). It orchestrates the SDK's pure API calls (campus.auth.sessions / logins / users / exchange_code_for_token) around Flask request state, so campus_python itself stays free of any web framework.

OAuthLoginManager wires this module in at init_app; apps never call it directly. The SDK's session-id provider seam is installed here, so the SDK resources resolve their ids from the same flask.session keys this module writes — during the rollout window both sides write identical values (idempotent), and after the SDK sheds its flask lane this module is the sole owner.

class UserCache:
    """Process-local cache of resolved session users (#57 semantics).

    Entries snapshot the user via to_resource() and are rehydrated per
    hit, so callers cannot poison the cache by mutating flask.g.user.
    """

    def __init__(self, ttl_seconds: float = USER_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS):
        self.ttl_seconds = ttl_seconds
        # (kind, session_id) -> (expires_at, user snapshot, device_id).
        self._entries: dict[
            tuple[str, str],
            tuple[float, object, str | None],
        ] = {}

    def get(
            self, kind: str, session_id: str | None
    ) -> tuple[object, str | None] | None:
        """The cached (user, device_id) for a session, or None.

        Expired entries are dropped lazily on read.
        """
        if session_id is None:
            return None
        entry = self._entries.get((kind, session_id))
        if entry is None:
            return None
        expires_at, snapshot, device_id = entry
        if time.monotonic() >= expires_at:
            self._entries.pop((kind, session_id), None)
            return None
        user = (
            campus.model.User.from_resource(snapshot)
            if isinstance(snapshot, dict)
            else snapshot
        )
        return user, device_id

    def put(
            self,
            kind: str,
            session_id: str | None,
            user: object,
            device_id: str | None,
    ) -> None:
        """Cache a session's resolved user for ttl_seconds."""
        if session_id is None:
            return
        snapshot: object = (
            user.to_resource()
            if isinstance(user, _Snapshottable)
            else user
        )
        self._entries[(kind, session_id)] = (
            time.monotonic() + self.ttl_seconds,
            snapshot,
            device_id,
        )

    def pop(self, kind: str, session_id: str | None) -> None:
        """Drop a session's cached user (logout, stale session)."""
        if session_id is not None:
            self._entries.pop((kind, session_id), None)

Resolved users are cached per session for UserCache's ttl (#57): warm requests make zero upstream calls. Trade-off: a session revoked server-side — not through logout(), which evicts immediately — keeps resolving for up to the TTL window.

Resolution failures degrade to anonymous (#28): a cookie whose session/login cannot be resolved — gone (404), denied (#854 owning-client checks), or unreachable (gateway 502, malformed response) — must never propagate out of this app-wide hook, or the browser is bricked on every route including /logout. def push_context(campus: campus_python.Campus, cache: UserCache) -> None:
    """Push auth/login context to flask.g (the SDK push_context port).

    Resolved users are cached per session for UserCache's ttl (#57):
    warm requests make zero upstream calls. Trade-off: a session
    revoked server-side — not through logout(), which evicts
    immediately — keeps resolving for up to the TTL window.

    Resolution failures degrade to anonymous (#28): a cookie whose
    session/login cannot be resolved — gone (404), denied (#854
    owning-client checks), or unreachable (gateway 502, malformed
    response) — must never propagate out of this app-wide hook, or
    the browser is bricked on every route including /logout. The
    reference is dropped and the request flows to the app's auth
    gate, which redirects to login.
    """
    flask.g.user = None
    flask.g.device = None

    # Try to load auth session if one exists
    if campus.auth.sessions.has_session():
        session_id = flask.session.get(SESSION_STORAGE_KEY)
        cached = cache.get(LANE_SESSION, session_id)
        if cached is not None:
            flask.g.user, flask.g.device = cached
            return
        try:
            auth_session = campus.auth.sessions.from_session()
            if auth_session.user_id:
                # The auth service embeds the session user for the
                # owning client (#879); the operator-gated users route
                # remains the fallback for older auth services.
                user = (
                    getattr(auth_session, "user", None)
                    or campus.auth.users[auth_session.user_id].get()
                )
                flask.g.user = user
                cache.put(LANE_SESSION, session_id, user, None)
        except campus_python.errors.NotFoundError:
            # Session no longer exists on server (expired, restart, etc.)
            _forget(cache, LANE_SESSION, session_id)
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.warning(
                f"Auth session resolution failed ({session_id}): "
                f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
            )
            _forget(cache, LANE_SESSION, session_id)

    # Try to load login session if one exists
    elif campus.auth.logins.has_session():
        login_id = flask.session.get(LOGIN_STORAGE_KEY)
        cached = cache.get(LANE_LOGIN, login_id)
        if cached is not None:
            flask.g.user, flask.g.device = cached
            return
        try:
            login_session = campus.auth.logins.from_session()
            login_user_id = login_session.user_id
            # Embedded login user (#879) with the same fallback.
            user = getattr(login_session, "user", None)
            if user is None and login_user_id is not None:
                user = campus.auth.users[login_user_id].get()
            flask.g.user = user
            flask.g.device = login_session.device_id
            if user is not None:
                cache.put(
                    LANE_LOGIN, login_id, user, login_session.device_id
                )
        except campus_python.errors.NotFoundError:
            # Login session no longer exists on server
            _forget(cache, LANE_LOGIN, login_id)
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.warning(
                f"Login session resolution failed ({login_id}): "
                f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
            )
            _forget(cache, LANE_LOGIN, login_id)

def start_login(
        campus: campus_python.Campus,
        target: str,
        scopes: list[str] | None = None,
) -> werkzeug.Response:
    """Begin an authorization flow (the SDK authorize port).

    Returns a redirect response to the Campus OAuth authorize endpoint.

    Args:
        campus: The Campus client.
        target: The OAuth callback URL the auth service redirects back
            to (the app's /finalize_login route).
        scopes: OAuth scopes to request for the minted user credential.
            None (the default) keeps ["campus.profile"]. Apps whose
            features need the signed-in user's token to carry
            management scopes — the capability leg of the #865/#883
            two-leg model, grant row AND token scope — pass the full
            list, e.g. ["campus.profile", "timetable:admin"].
            campus.auth validates requested scopes against the minting
            client's allowed_scopes cap fail-closed (RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1
            semantics), so extend the client's cap BEFORE deploying a
            wider request. Scopes ride the auth session into the
            exchanged token (requested_scopes = authsession.scopes),
            so this list is exactly what lands on the user's stored
            credential.

    IMPORTANT: This returns a redirect response directly (never fetches
    via requests) to preserve the browser's user agent and cookies. If
    we proxied through requests, Google detects a server user agent and
    switches to OAuth Lite flow which breaks in browsers (500 error).
    """
    from urllib.parse import urlencode

    auth_session = campus.auth.sessions.new(
        redirect_uri=target,
        scopes=scopes or DEFAULT_LOGIN_SCOPES,
        target=target,
    )
    # Context owns the storage key; the SDK's new() writes the same key
    # with the same value during the compat window (idempotent).
    flask.session[SESSION_STORAGE_KEY] = auth_session.id
    authorize_url = campus.auth.base_url + campus.auth.make_path("authorize")
    params = {
        "client_id": env.CLIENT_ID,
        "response_type": "code",  # OAuth2 authorization code flow
        "redirect_uri": target,  # Callback URL after auth
        "state": auth_session.id,
    }
    return flask.redirect(f"{authorize_url}?{urlencode(params)}")

def finalize_login(
        campus: campus_python.Campus,
        *,
        state: str,
        code: str,
        scope: str,
) -> None:
    """Complete an authorization flow (the SDK finalize port).

    Steps: validate the auth session, exchange the code (credentials
    are stored server-side by the token endpoint), finalize the
    session, provision the user, create the login session — the
    device id rides the auth session (#825: campus.auth observed the
    campus_device cookie at /authorize; the minted fallback keeps
    non-cookie flows working).

    Raises:
        campus_python.errors.BadRequestError / AuthenticationError:
            rejected codes (replayed, expired) or a state mismatch —
            routine in a browser flow; callers send the user back to
            sign-in (#690).

    Args:
        state: The OAuth state parameter (the auth session id).
        code: The authorization code from the OAuth callback.
        scope: Granted OAuth scopes (accepted for flow compatibility;
            the grant itself is recorded server-side).
    """
    # 1. Validate auth session
    auth_session = campus.auth.sessions.from_code(code=code)
    if auth_session.id != state:
        raise campus_python.errors.AuthenticationError(
            error_description="State parameter does not match session ID."
        )
    if auth_session.user_id is None:
        raise campus_python.errors.AuthenticationError(
            error_description="Unidentified user from auth session"
        )

    # 2. Exchange authorization code for access token
    campus.auth.exchange_code_for_token(
        code=code,
        redirect_uri=auth_session.redirect_uri,
    )

    # 3. Finalize session; the response embeds the session user for
    # the owning client (#879). Pre-#879 services return no user.
    _target, session_user = campus.auth.sessions[auth_session.id].finalize()

    # 4. Ensure user exists (the server provisions the user record
    # during verify_login; a missing user is a hard error here).
    if session_user is None:
        campus.auth.users[auth_session.user_id].get()

    # The auth session is consumed — clear its storage key (the SDK's
    # finalize() pops the same key during the compat window).
    flask.session.pop(SESSION_STORAGE_KEY, None)

    # 5. Create the login session
    login_session = campus.auth.logins.new(
        user_id=auth_session.user_id,
        device_id=(
            auth_session.device_id
            or uid.generate_category_uid("device", length=16)
        ),
        agent_string=flask.request.headers.get("User-Agent", ""),
    )
    flask.session[LOGIN_STORAGE_KEY] = login_session.id

def logout(
        campus: campus_python.Campus,
        cache: UserCache | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Logout the current user (the SDK logout port).

    Revokes the login session through the API, then clears local
    state. Remote revocation is best-effort: the login session may
    already be gone server-side (expired, swept, or the client's auth
    service session cookie lost across app workers), but the local
    session state is always cleared so the user is signed out locally
    regardless of the revocation outcome.
    """
    flask.g.pop("user", None)
    flask.g.pop("device", None)
    if not campus.auth.logins.has_session():
        return
    try:
        login_session = campus.auth.logins.from_session()
        campus.auth.logins[login_session.id].revoke()
        if cache is not None:
            cache.pop(LANE_LOGIN, login_session.id)
    except Exception as err:
        logger.warning(
            "Login session revocation failed (continuing with local "
            "logout): %s", err
        )
        flask.session.pop(LOGIN_STORAGE_KEY, None)
    # The SDK's revoke() pops the same key during the compat window;
    # this module is the owner, so clear it unconditionally.
    flask.session.pop(LOGIN_STORAGE_KEY, None)
